newsitem.title: USA: Philadelphia Fed sees U.S. '97 GDP up 2.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philadelphia Fed sees U.S. '97 GDP up 2.7 pct.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia said on Wednesday forecasters polled in its quarterly survey expected the U.S. Gross Domestic Product to grow by 2.7 percent in 1997 while the Consumer Price Index would rise by 3.0 percent and the unemployment rate would average 5.3 percent.

"On a year-over-year basis, the forecasters expect real GDP to grow at a rate of 2.7 percent in 1997, up from their expectation of 2.3 percent in last quarter's survey," the Philadelphia Fed said. "Growth will decelerate to an annual rate of 2.1 percent in 1998."

"Inflation, as measured by the CPI, will average 3.0 percent at an annual rate in the first quarter and hold steady at that rate through the third quarter," the bank also said. "On a fourth-quarter-over-fourth-quarter basis, CPI inflation will hold steady at 3.0 percent over the next two years."

The consensus of the 38 forecasters polled by the Philadelphia Fed also said "the unemployment rate is expected to remain within a range of 5.3 to 5.4 percent over the next five quarters. On an annual-average basis, the unemployment rate is expected to average 5.3 percent in 1997 and 5.4 percent in 1998."
Other forecasts in the survey expected:
-- GDP growth up 2.2 percent in the first quarter of 1997
-- CPI up 3.0 percent in the first quarter
-- GDP price index up 2.3 percent in 1997 and up 2.5 percent in 1998
-- The rate on three-month Treasury bills to hold steady within a range of 5.0 to 5.1 percent over the next five quarters.
-- The 10-year Treasury bond yield to fall to 6.3 percent in the third quarter of 1997, and hold steady at 6.3 percent through the first quarter of 1998.
